protocol.instrument_name: Queensland Community Pharmacy Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis - Clinical Practice Guideline
protocol.legal_basis: Not stated in this document; issued by Queensland Health as a Queensland Community Pharmacy clinical practice guideline for a prescribing service (page 1).
protocol.supervision_model: Document's own terminology: pharmacists are advised to 'exercise professional discretion and judgement' and to make decisions 'in consultation with the patient and/or their parent/caregiver'; pharmacists must prescribe according to 'the specified sections of the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines'. No 'collaborative'/'autonomous' label is printed.
protocol.scope_summary: Clinical practice guideline for Queensland community pharmacists covering assessment, differentiation and management of allergic and nonallergic rhinitis: patient history, physical examination, Table 1 symptom differentiation, non-pharmacological measures, pharmacotherapy delegated to the current online Therapeutic Guidelines, 'Refer when' triggers, patient advice and 4-week clinical review. It is not a dosing protocol: no strength, dose, frequency or quantity is printed anywhere in the document.

nasal polyps or other structural abnormalities

exclusion_exceptions.text: Ineligibility for treatment as part of a prescribing service does not preclude a patient from accessing services provided as part of usual pharmacy care.

diagnosis_pathways.name: Allergic and Nonallergic Rhinitis - assessment and management pathway

steps.description: Obtain sufficient information from the patient to assess the safety and appropriateness of any recommendations and medicines. The patient history should consider: age; pregnancy and lactation status (if applicable); onset, nature, duration, frequency, severity and pattern of respiratory symptoms.

Patient history continues: other signs and symptoms suggestive of infection including fever, purulent nasal discharge or facial pain; respiratory virus testing (PCR or RAT) and results; presence of asthma symptoms; co-existing and underlying medical conditions including asthma, nasal polyps or other allergic diseases (e.g., atopic dermatitis); family history of nasal polyps or allergic disease (including rhinitis); triggering, aggravating and relieving factors (e.g., occupational exposure to cleaning chemicals, foods, pollen, cigarette smoke); emotional and social impacts of the condition; current and recently ceased treatments (including prescribed medicines, vitamins, herbs, other supplements and over-the-counter medicines); pharmacological and non-pharmacological strategies tried to treat current symptoms, and response, including use of nasal decongestants; drug allergies/adverse drug reactions; smoking status.

Use Table 1. Symptoms and clinical signs of rhinitis to differentiate allergic from non-allergic rhinitis. Allergic rhinitis: symptoms after exposure to animals, pollen, dust or other environmental factors/allergens - sneezing; nasal congestion; clear rhinorrhoea; upper airway cough syndrome (post-nasal drip); mucosal itching of the nose, eyes, ears and palate. Non-specific symptoms: 'fuzzy' head; tiredness and daytime sleepiness; constant 'colds'. Non-allergic rhinitis: symptoms without an identifiable infectious or allergic cause - nasal blockage and/or congestion; clear rhinorrhoea; post-nasal drip. May or may not be present: sneezing; itchy nose, ears or throat. Symptoms may present sporadically at any time of the year, although they may be exacerbated by environmental factors such as barometric pressure or temperature changes, bright lights or physical irritants. Allergic conjunctivitis frequently co-occurs (eye redness, watering and itching). In children, additional symptoms may include sniffing, blinking and eye rubbing, speech problems, snoring, mouth breathing, and dark undereye circles. (Column attribution of the last two statements is uncertain in the text extraction - see open_questions.)

gates.criterion: Rhinitis type classified as allergic or nonallergic from symptoms and clinical signs

provenance.section_heading: Table 1. Symptoms and clinical signs of rhinitis

steps.description: Reported symptom improvement with second generation antihistamines is strongly suggestive of allergic rhinitis, as is a previous response to intranasal corticosteroids (6).

steps.description: Physical examination of nose, throat, eyes and ears is generally required (5). Where appropriate, palpate the neck for lymphadenopathy (more relevant when throat symptoms present). Where appropriate, conduct an assessment of vital signs. Outward signs of rhinitis upon examination may include: enlarged/swelled, pale, boggy nasal mucosa with thin secretions; nasal polyps; dark undereye area due to venous congestion (particularly in children); cobblestone throat due to irritation of post-nasal drip; mouth breathing (6).

Patients with symptoms of asthma or lower respiratory disease should have a chest examination in accordance with the clinical protocol for the Queensland Community Pharmacy Improved Asthma Symptom Control Program.

gates.criterion: Symptoms of asthma or lower respiratory disease present

steps.description: Develop management plan: Pharmacists must ensure that they are prescribing medicines according to the specified sections of the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines.

gates.criterion: Prescribing aligns with the specified sections of the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines

steps.description: Allergic rhinitis - Pharmacist management of allergic rhinitis involves: developing a treatment plan based on the Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy: Allergic Rhinitis Treatment Plan (10); non-pharmacological measures: education regarding allergen avoidance and minimising exposure to known/clinically obvious allergens and irritants if possible, as per the Australian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy: Allergic Rhinitis Clinical Update 2024 (4); nasal irrigation with saline to soothe nasal passages, and clear mucous and irritants (11).

Allergic rhinitis (continues from page 4): Advice to patients that oral and intranasal decongestants have no role in the management of allergic rhinitis. Use of intranasal decongestants for more than 3–5 days causes rebound congestion (rhinitis medicamentosa). Prolonged use of oral decongestants can increase blood pressure and the risk of arrythmias in people with cardiovascular disease (1). Pharmacotherapy NB1: A medicine mentioned in the Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory (Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis - Allergic rhinitis), including eye drops for allergic conjunctivitis(1). NB1: Anti-inflammatory eye drops (e.g., ketorolac and corticosteroids) are mentioned within the Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory (Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis - Allergic rhinitis) for use under specialist advice only and are not authorised for use by pharmacists; these are not indicated for the initial management of allergic conjunctivitis. Vasoconstrictor eye drops (e.g., naphazoline and tetryzoline) are also not indicated for allergic conjunctivitis.

Nonallergic rhinitis - Pharmacist management of nonallergic rhinitis involves: non-pharmacological measures: education regarding avoidance and minimisation of exposure to known/clinically obvious irritants where possible; nasal irrigation with saline to soothe dry nasal passages, and clear out mucous (12). Pharmacotherapy: A medicine mentioned in Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory (Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis - Nonallergic rhinitis) (9). Intranasal corticosteroids are the mainstay of treatment for nonallergic rhinitis (9).

Confirm management is appropriate: Pharmacists must consult the Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook and other resources to confirm that management is appropriate, including for: contraindications and precautions; drug interactions; pregnancy and lactation.

gates.criterion: Contraindications and precautions, drug interactions, and pregnancy and lactation confirmed appropriate against Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook and other resources

steps.description: Communicate agreed management plan: Comprehensive advice and counselling (including supporting written information when required) should be provided to the patient regarding: individual product and medicine use e.g., dosing and correct intranasal spray technique; non-pharmacological measures; how to manage adverse effects; when to seek further care and/or treatment; when to return for follow-up.

Communicate agreed management plan (continues from page 5): It is the pharmacist's responsibility to ensure the suitability and accuracy of any resources provided to patients (and/or parents/caregivers), and to ensure these comply with all copyright conditions. The agreed management plan should be shared with members of the patient's multidisciplinary healthcare team, with the patient's consent.

General advice: At the time of initial consultation, patients (and/or parents/caregivers) should be advised to see an appropriate healthcare provider if: the condition does not improve within 4 weeks of starting treatment; the patient's condition worsens, including developing systemic signs and symptoms; the patient develops new signs or symptoms (e.g. infection); the patient develops new, or worsening, asthma symptoms; quality of life is significantly affected; adverse effects of treatment cannot be managed in the pharmacy setting. (Each trigger is captured as a red flag; escalation destination is 'an appropriate healthcare provider'.)

Clinical review: Clinical review with the pharmacist (or the patient's chosen healthcare provider) should occur in line with recommendations in the Therapeutic Guidelines. Patients should return for a follow-up consultation 4 weeks after initiation of intranasal corticosteroids to assess for: response to treatment and if changes to the treatment plan are required (continue, modify, stop and/or refer); intranasal spray administration technique. If the patient's symptoms are mild and adequately managed with an oral or intranasal antihistamine after trialling a new treatment for 4 weeks, clinical review will generally not be required, and the patient may be advised to remain on the minimum effective dose. For patients continuing therapy, follow-up should be individualised to the patient's clinical presentation, response to treatment, and therapeutic goals.

Supply quantity rule: Pharmacists should prescribe a quantity of medicine (including repeats), that aligns with the expected duration of therapy, ensuring sufficient supply until the patient's next review. The total quantity prescribed should not exceed 12 months' supply (including repeats).

open_questions.observed: The guideline has 'Guideline overview', 'Refer when', 'Treat (if clinically appropriate) and concurrently refer', assessment, management and review sections, but no inclusion-criteria section. inclusion[] left empty rather than inferred; see EXE-1 for the ineligibility statement.
open_questions.why_unclear: Spec forbids fabricating criteria; the document prints only referral/escalation situations.

open_questions.observed: 'Refer the patient to an appropriate healthcare provider (including emergency services, if required) in the following situations:' followed by 7 bullets, read as independent (any_of) triggers; each bullet is mirrored as a separate red flag. No AND grouping and no explicit combinatorics is printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: Document does not state all_of/any_of; any_of chosen because each bullet reads as a standalone referral situation.

open_questions.observed: The document labels these situations 'Refer when', not 'exclusion criteria'. They are transcribed into eligibility.exclusion because they remove the patient from management within the prescribing service (p.1: 'Ineligibility for treatment as part of a prescribing service does not preclude a patient from accessing services provided as part of usual pharmacy care'). 'Treat and concurrently refer' situations (RF-8, RF-9) are kept as red flags only, not exclusions, because treatment proceeds.
open_questions.why_unclear: Framing of refer-when lists as exclusions is an interpretation; recorded for review.

open_questions.observed: No minimum or maximum age is printed for rhinitis eligibility. The only numeric age rule is 'asthma in patients under the age of 16 years' -> refer (p.2). age_bounds recorded as null/null with provenance at the Refer when section.
open_questions.why_unclear: Document states no numeric age bound for the guideline population.

open_questions.observed: The text extraction interleaves the 'Allergic rhinitis' and 'Non-allergic rhinitis' columns. 'Allergic conjunctivitis frequently co-occurs (eye redness, watering and itching)' and 'In children, additional symptoms may include sniffing, blinking and eye rubbing, speech problems, snoring, mouth breathing, and dark undereye circles' appear within the non-allergic column flow of the extracted text but read as applying to allergic rhinitis / to rhinitis generally.
open_questions.why_unclear: Table layout cannot be confirmed from the text extraction; both readings recorded rather than silently reconciled (spec rule 2).

open_questions.observed: The document presents parallel 'Allergic rhinitis' (p.4-5) and 'Nonallergic rhinitis' (p.5) management sections but prints no explicit branch or on-fail instructions. Gates 'on_fail: SEE_PW-1-S10' / 'SEE_PW-1-S8' were inferred from classification of the rhinitis type.
open_questions.why_unclear: Branch routing is implied by the two management sections, not stated as a rule.

open_questions.observed: Key points (p.2) classify rhinitis as 'allergic, nonallergic (vasomotor), infectious, drug-induced and occupational', but management sections are provided only for allergic and nonallergic rhinitis. No management steps are printed for infectious, drug-induced or occupational rhinitis; referral criteria cover infection and a medicine that can cause or exacerbate rhinitis.
open_questions.why_unclear: Guideline does not state how those subtypes are to be managed inside the service.

open_questions.observed: No strength, dose, frequency, quantity or duration is printed anywhere in the guideline. Pharmacotherapy is delegated to 'A medicine mentioned in the Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory (...)' and to 'the specified sections of the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Dosing detail does not exist in the source; treatment rows intentionally left blank rather than filled from outside sources.

open_questions.observed: Document gives a single referral wording - 'Refer the patient to an appropriate healthcare provider (including emergency services, if required)' - plus patient advice to 'see an appropriate healthcare provider'. It does not define separate routine/urgent/emergency destinations; urgent[] left empty and emergency[] holds only the printed 'emergency services, if required'.
open_questions.why_unclear: No tiered referral destinations are printed.

open_questions.observed: 'Patients with symptoms of asthma or lower respiratory disease should have a chest examination in accordance with the clinical protocol for the Queensland Community Pharmacy Improved Asthma Symptom Control Program.' What to do when those symptoms are absent is not stated; gate on_fail recorded as 'unclear'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Document states the positive condition only.

open_questions.observed: 'Pharmacists must ensure that they are prescribing medicines according to the specified sections of the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines' (p.4) and 'Confirm management is appropriate ... contraindications and precautions; drug interactions; pregnancy and lactation' (p.5) do not state an on-fail action; both gates recorded as on_fail 'unclear'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Spec requires on_fail; document does not say what happens on failure.

open_questions.observed: Whole document reviewed (pp.1-9): no notifiable condition, GP notification, AIR entry or other notification requirement is mentioned. notifiable.required recorded as null.
open_questions.why_unclear: Document is silent; no page can be cited for a positive requirement.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Legal basis for pharmacist prescribing under this guideline (regulation / poisons schedule provision) is not printed - confirm the QLD jurisdictional basis before go-live.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Spec requires legal_basis; the document only identifies itself as a Queensland Community Pharmacy clinical practice guideline printed by Queensland Health.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Supervision model: document says pharmacists should 'exercise professional discretion and judgement' in consultation with the patient/parent/caregiver and must prescribe per the current online Therapeutic Guidelines - confirm whether the service is 'collaborative' or 'autonomous' in Queensland terms.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: No 'collaborative'/'autonomous' terminology is printed; description uses the document's own wording only.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Pin the exact version/date of the 'current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines' (and the Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory rhinitis topics) that the prescribing service links to.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The guideline delegates all medicine selection/dosing to an unpinned online resource, so the operative content can change independently of this document.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Eye-drop authorisation boundary: 'Anti-inflammatory eye drops (e.g., ketorolac and corticosteroids) ... are not authorised for use by pharmacists' and 'Vasoconstrictor eye drops ... are also not indicated for allergic conjunctivitis' - confirm how the module enforces this prohibition.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Explicit non-authorisation statement inside the protocol must be enforced as a hard block, not a soft prompt.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Chest examination for asthma/lower respiratory disease symptoms depends on 'the clinical protocol for the Queensland Community Pharmacy Improved Asthma Symptom Control Program' - confirm the interlock/hand-off between the two programs.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Cross-program dependency; this document does not reproduce that protocol's content.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Supply quantity ceiling: 'The total quantity prescribed should not exceed 12 months' supply (including repeats)' - confirm local interpretation of a 12-month total supply and repeats handling.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Quantity rule is stated without per-medicine detail and touches local supply policy.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Referral destinations: document says only 'an appropriate healthcare provider' - confirm the local list of acceptable destinations (GP, ENT, paediatrician, emergency department, other) for each red flag.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Destination specificity is left to local policy; the document names no destination types beyond 'emergency services, if required'.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Pregnancy/lactation handling: document requires checking 'contraindications and precautions, drug interactions, pregnancy and lactation' against Therapeutic Guidelines/AMH but prints no rhinitis-specific pregnancy or lactation guidance - confirm the local rule set.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Pregnancy/lactation caveat is delegated to external resources; nothing verbatim exists in this document to embed.
